name: Puerto Rico
summary: From Spanish colony to a U.S. territory, without independence.
notes: The 1598 English occupation concerned San Juan. Commonwealth status in 1952 established local constitutional government, not sovereignty outside the United States.

events.title: A Spanish claim to Borikén
events.detail: Columbus reached the island on his second voyage.
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: Spanish colonization begins
events.detail: Juan Ponce de León established Caparra; Taíno resistance followed.

events.title: English forces occupy San Juan
events.detail: The Earl of Cumberland captured the capital but disease forced withdrawal. The whole island did not change hands.

events.title: U.S. administration takes over
events.detail: Spanish forces evacuated and U.S. military government began after the Spanish–American War.

events.title: Cession to the United States takes effect
events.detail: Ratifications of the December 1898 Treaty of Paris were exchanged, transferring sovereignty.

events.title: Commonwealth constitution
events.detail: Puerto Rico’s constitution took effect while the island remained a U.S. territory.
